newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban advance in northeastern province.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban advance in northeastern province.

text.p: Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban militia captured parts of the northeastern province of Takhar on Wednesday, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) reported that the militia was battling its way towards the provincial capital, Taloqan, which president Burhanuddin Rabbani and Ittehad-i-Islami chief Abdurrab Rasul Sayyaf have used as a temporary base since the Taleban drove the Rabbani government from Kabul in September.
AIP said the Taleban had launched a major offensive into Takhar from neighbouring Kunduz province on Tuesday evening.

By Wednesday morning they had captured Khwaja Ghar and Bangi districts, and were advancing towards Taloqan, about 30 km (19 miles) east of Bangi. The militia had earlier seized the Qabr-i-Qazi district, east of Kunduz, AIP said.
It said the Taleban had killed 20 soldiers loyal to former government military commander Ahmed Shah Masood and captured 285 after intense fighting in which the Taleban lost eight dead.
AIP said local commanders had joined the Taleban offensive, swelling the militia's ranks to 1,500 from an initial 1,000 and white Taleban flags were flying in many parts of the province.
AIP said two helicopters had taken off from Taloqan for an undisclosed destination on Tuesday, apparently with opposition leaders on board, but it could not identify them.
No other reports of the fighting were immediately available.
